name: N25 FENCE_OPEN: indent capped at 4096
why: a line with 5,000 or more blanks before the run stops being a fence; only the accepted-line row (5,000 to 200,000 characters) reads one, because every other comparison stops at 1,000 characters or 100 blanks and the 50,000-character lines are only timed. A cap is the obvious other cure for a quadratic regex.

name: N26 FENCE_OPEN: indent also reads a vertical tab
why: a vertical tab before a fence is read as part of the indent; no alphabet held one before the exotic-blank enumeration

name: N28 FENCE_OPEN: run capped at 4096
why: a run of 4,097 or more fence characters stops being a fence (the run capped); only the accepted-line row sees it

name: N42 INDENTED: indent capped at 4096
why: the INDENTED indent capped at 4,096 characters: a line of 5,000 or more blanks before a cell fence stops being one

name: N43 INDENTED: indent without a vertical tab

name: N44 INDENTED: indent without a byte order mark
why: the INDENTED indent without a byte order mark (a U+FEFF in front of a cell fence stops being one); only the exotic-blank enumeration reads one

name: N45 INDENTED: indent spelled out
why: the INDENTED indent spelled out as ASCII blanks, CR, LF, NBSP, U+2028 and U+2029: loses the vertical tab, the byte order mark, U+3000 and the other Unicode spaces

name: N53 INDENTED: run capped at 4096
